2.old: North Maple Ridge is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Maple Ridge doesn’t publish a boundary for it. The City’s neighbourhood list names Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Ruskin, Silver Valley, Thornhill, Town Centre, Webster’s Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon, with no north area.
2.new: North Maple Ridge is a sub-area name used in the MLS®, and the City of Maple Ridge has no published boundary for it. Looking at the City’s neighbourhood list, you will find Yennadon, Whonnock, Webster’s Corners, Town Centre, Thornhill, Silver Valley, Ruskin, Port Haney, Port Hammond and Albion/Kanaka, but no north area.

18.old: Route 733 runs between Haney Place and Rock Ridge Drive at 133 Avenue, going up 232 Street from Dewdney Trunk Road. Some weekday trips continue to or start from Port Haney Station
18.new: Route 733 connects Haney Place with Rock Ridge Drive at 133 Avenue, heading up 232 Street after leaving Dewdney Trunk Road. A few weekday trips either carry on to Port Haney Station or begin there

20.old: Route 741 runs between Haney Place and Anderson Creek Drive at 232 Street. Going out it uses 227 Street, 128 Avenue, 232 Street, 136 Avenue and 137 Avenue, and coming back it uses 141 Avenue and Silver Valley Road. Some weekday trips continue to or start from Port Haney Station
20.new: Some weekday trips begin at or continue to Port Haney Station. Route 741 links Haney Place with Anderson Creek Drive at 232 Street. Outbound the bus follows 227 Street, then 128 Avenue, then 232 Street, then 136 Avenue and 137 Avenue; inbound it follows 141 Avenue and Silver Valley Road.

50.old: Maple Ridge is in School District 42 (SD42). Names, grades and addresses from the Province’s Maple Ridge school list and SD42. Checked against the official pages on October 17, 2026.
50.new: School District 42 (SD42) covers Maple Ridge. SD42 and the Province’s list of Maple Ridge schools supply the names, grades and addresses; the official pages were consulted on October 17, 2026 to verify them.

87.old: On the South Alouette River at the corner of 232 Street and 132 Avenue. Each fall the river welcomes large populations of spawning pink and chum salmon
87.new: It is on the South Alouette River, where 232 Street meets 132 Avenue. Spawning pink and chum salmon gather in large numbers in the river each fall

89.old: A playground completed in fall 2024, a spray park completed in July 2025, a zipline, a picnic shelter and an off-leash dog area at 13165 236 Street
89.new: At 13165 236 Street are an off-leash dog area, a zipline and a picnic shelter, along with a playground finished in fall 2024 and a spray park finished in July 2025.

95.old: The Silver Valley trails were originally developed as horse trails. They are now shared by walkers, hikers, recreational cyclists and equestrian riders
95.new: Silver Valley’s trails began as horse trails. Today walkers, hikers, recreational cyclists and equestrian riders all share them

101.old: Canyon Trail runs from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls, 1.2 km one way with some challenging hills. The flat Riverfront Trails are 3 km one way
101.new: Canyon Trail covers 1.2 km one way between the fish hatchery and Cliff Falls, and some of the hills are challenging. The Riverfront Trails are flat and 3 km one way

124.old: In the downtown core on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, beside City Hall, the Leisure Centre, the Greg Moore Youth Centre, the ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall
124.new: Found downtown on 224 Street, between Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway. Its neighbours are Haney Place Mall, the ACT Arts Centre, the Greg Moore Youth Centre, the Leisure Centre and City Hall

160.old: The City says it adopted updates to the Official Community Plan and to the Town Centre, Hammond, Silver Valley and Albion area plans in 2025. Albion’s was adopted on October 28 and the others in November.
160.new: According to the City, in 2025 it adopted updates to its Official Community Plan as well as the area plans for Town Centre, Hammond, Silver Valley and Albion. The Albion plan was adopted on October 28, while the rest followed in November.

161.old: The City adopted the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan on January 27, 2026 as Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021. It covers Lougheed Highway from Maple Meadows Way to 221 Street.
161.new: The Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan was adopted by the City on January 27, 2026 under Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021. Its area follows Lougheed Highway between Maple Meadows Way and 221 Street.

164.old: The City publishes a North and South Alouette River Floodplain Map and a Fraser River Floodplain Map, and says a floodplain map outlines the area expected to flood on average once every 200 years.
164.new: Two floodplain maps are published by the City: one for the North and South Alouette River and one for the Fraser River. A floodplain map, the City says, outlines the area expected to flood once every 200 years on average.

165.old: The City monitors rainfall and water levels in the Fraser River, the North and South Alouette River and Kanaka Creek.
165.new: Rainfall and water levels on Kanaka Creek, the Fraser River and the North and South Alouette River are monitored by the City.

166.old: The City says some parts of Maple Ridge face landslides and debris flows, and that melting snowpacks combined with warm weather can create landslides.
166.new: Landslides and debris flows are a risk in some parts of Maple Ridge, the City says, and it adds that snowpack melt during warm weather can set off landslides.

168.old: The West Coast Express has two Maple Ridge stops, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station, with five trips daily, leaving Maple Ridge in the morning and returning in the evening, Monday to Friday.
168.new: Maple Ridge has two West Coast Express stops, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station. There are five trips a day, Monday to Friday: they leave Maple Ridge in the morning and come back in the evening.

169.old: TransLink’s Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit line would run 22 km with 13 stations and service every 10 minutes at peak. TransLink says it is in detailed planning with preliminary funding through the 2025 Investment Plan, and that more funding is needed to deliver it.
169.new: The Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit line proposed by TransLink would be 22 km long, with 13 stations and a bus every 10 minutes at peak. It is in detailed planning, TransLink says, and has preliminary funding from the 2025 Investment Plan, but more funding is needed to build it.

199.old: Route 733 runs between Haney Place and Rock Ridge Drive at 133 Avenue, going up 232 Street from Dewdney Trunk Road. Some weekday trips continue to or start from Port Haney Station.
199.new: Route 733 links Rock Ridge Drive at 133 Avenue to Haney Place, following 232 Street up from Dewdney Trunk Road. Port Haney Station is the end or the start of some weekday trips.

200.old: Route 741 runs between Haney Place and Anderson Creek Drive at 232 Street. Going out it uses 227 Street, 128 Avenue, 232 Street, 136 Avenue and 137 Avenue, and coming back it uses 141 Avenue and Silver Valley Road. Some weekday trips continue to or start from Port Haney Station.
200.new: Route 741 serves Anderson Creek Drive at 232 Street and Haney Place. Heading out it takes 227 Street, then 128 Avenue and 232 Street, followed by 136 Avenue and 137 Avenue. On the return it takes 141 Avenue and Silver Valley Road. A number of weekday trips start from or continue on to Port Haney Station.

201.old: The West Coast Express has two Maple Ridge stops, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station, with five trips daily, leaving Maple Ridge in the morning and returning in the evening, Monday to Friday.
201.new: Riders can use either of the two Maple Ridge stops on the West Coast Express, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station. Five trips run each weekday, heading out in the morning and coming back in the evening.

209.old: The Maple Ridge Public Library is at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, and it is the only Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in Maple Ridge.
209.new: Maple Ridge’s only Fraser Valley Regional Library branch is the Maple Ridge Public Library, at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road.

214.old: The City publishes a North and South Alouette River Floodplain Map and a Fraser River Floodplain Map, and says a floodplain map outlines the area expected to flood on average once every 200 years.
214.new: The City’s floodplain maps for Maple Ridge cover the North and South Alouette River and the Fraser River. A floodplain map, as the City describes it, outlines the area expected to flood once in every 200 years on average.

215.old: The City says some parts of Maple Ridge face landslides and debris flows, and that melting snowpacks combined with warm weather can create landslides.
215.new: According to the City, parts of Maple Ridge can see landslides and debris flows, and warm weather that melts the snowpack can bring landslides on as well.
